title: Weekly pilot triage: private/VPC latency & routing
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on VPC networking anomalies and p95 latency spikes after kernel upgrade candidate. SE triaged routing mismatches between private control plane and on-prem workers; next steps include targeted benchmark, MTU check, and a dry-run kernel rollout in staging. Action items assigned for logs, firewall rules, and scheduling maintenance window.
topics: p95 latency regression after 2025-05 kernel candidate
intermittent 502s routed through ALB/NLB when failover occurs
MTU and fragmentation concerns across Azure/VPC peer link
fallback routing policy to hosted when private capacity low
next tests: end-to-end 90/95 latency benchmarks and KV cache validation
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining on time. I think we can start. Uh quick roll call?
[00:08] Sarah - TheraScale: Sarah here.
[00:10] Rajat - TheraScale: Rajat here.
[00:12] Ethan - TheraScale: Ethan.
[00:15] Priya - TheraScale: Priya.
[00:17] Aisha: Great, Connor and Miguel and Lina from Redwood too?
[00:20] Connor (Redwood SE): Present.
[00:22] Miguel (Redwood SRE): yep, Miguel.
[00:24] Lina (CS): Lina.
[00:26] Aisha: Okay, agenda: latency triage, routing fallback, and plan for a staged kernel rollout in staging before prod.
[00:33] Sarah: Sounds good. We've been seeing a couple of p95 spikes in the last two weeks, especially after the 2025-05-28 kernel candidate that Connor sent over. Not sure if it's networking or the runtime.
[00:44] Connor: Right, we noticed a small repro in our lab where under mixed short-and-long inference workloads, the continuous batching path plus the new kernel's I/O path can add jitter. But your telemetry shows networking amplification too, so we need to separate those signals.
[00:57] Rajat: Quick note: we saw several 502s when the NLB rebalanced across AZs at around 03:40 UTC last Thursday. The control plane showed a fallback to hosted for about 90 seconds.
[01:12] Miguel: When fallback happened, logs show the on-prem workers timing out on KV fetches. Could be MTU or packet fragmentation on the cross-site link.
[01:23] Ethan: We actually changed MTU last month to 1450 for the peering tunnel to avoid PMTU blackhole. Maybe there's inconsistent MTU on the path.
[01:33] Priya: Also, we've seen increased token tail latency when the KV cache miss rate increased during traffic bursts. Could be two separate problems.
[01:42] Connor: Agreed, we'll run an isolated benchmark: pure local inference (no network), inference with KMS disabled, and inference through VPC to isolate kernel vs network.
[01:51] Aisha: Let's talk specifics — Connor, what's the immediate hypothesis and what we need from TheraScale?
[01:58] Connor: Hypothesis A: kernel candidate introduced small locking on the KV cache serialization path causing p95 to move up by ~40-80ms under mixed batches. Hypothesis B: path MTU/fragmentation causing occasional retransmits adding 200-400ms on tails. We need packet captures around a spike, and a list of firewall rules and load balancer idle timeout.
[02:20] Sarah: We can provide tcpdump around next spike, but it's intermittent. Should we turn on additional sampling?
[02:27] Miguel: Yes, enable packet capture on the worker host plus the VPC router for 1 minute when you see a spike. Also capture netstat/droplist from the NLB.
[02:38] Rajat: Our NLB is set to cross-zone, TCP idle 350s. We haven't changed it recently.
[02:44] Aisha: Could the idle timeout be causing connections to re-establish and cold starts blow up latency?
[02:50] Priya: Possibly, but the spike correlates with KV cache eviction windows (we configured small prefix cache TTLs for testing).
[02:58] Connor: Ok so let's map: TTL evictions could cause cache miss storms which exercise the I/O path and highlight kernel locking. Meanwhile, an MTU problem would show retransmits in tcpdump.
[03:10] Ethan: On our side, we will schedule a 15-minute sampling window with tcpdump and CPU memstat snapshots. Could we get a script from Redwood to run the focused bench?
[03:19] Connor: Yes — I'll upload a small bench harness that runs a controlled mix of short prompt and long prompt requests, with flags to enable/disable prefix cache and to log KV timings.
[03:29] Aisha: Good. Also, there were a few comments in the last runbook about fallback routing: when private capacity drops, the control plane currently prefers hosted variants but sometimes routes half the flow and that creates inconsistent session affinity.
[03:44] Miguel: That was an older policy bug; we patched the balancing heuristic but it only rolled out to the EU pool. The US pools still have the old algorithm that can split sticky sessions across hosted and private.
[03:56] Sarah: That explains the 90-second fallback Rajat mentioned — ephemeral sessions got split mid-request.
[04:03] Connor: We'll push the balancing fix to your staging pool tomorrow, but we should also add a deterministic fallback policy for long-running streams so we preserve session affinity.
[04:15] Rajat: Can you explain the deterministic fallback?
[04:18] Connor: If a request has streaming or long-running session flags, we only fallback to hosted if the entire private endpoint is unhealthy or throttled; we avoid split flows in the middle. It's just a configuration toggle.
[04:30] Aisha: Action item: Redwood to share the config diff and recommended settings for long-stream affinity.
[04:36] Sarah: Noted.
[04:38] [05:00] — five minute jump —
[05:00] Priya: Quick question about KMS — we run a customer-managed key in AWS KMS for payload encryption. When you fallback to hosted do you use the hosted KM? Is there a re-encrypt step?
[05:12] Miguel: Good flag — we don't re-encrypt; fallback uses an ephemeral transport layer. However, if a customer uses CMK with strict deny on cross-account usage, fallback won't be permitted. We can simulate fallback in a test account.
[05:26] Rajat: So for our pilot we want to keep CMK locked down, so fallback should be logger-only and not auto-route to hosted.
[05:34] Aisha: We'll make that a policy. Redwood will add a pilot toggle: "no-remote-fallback-without-cmk-share".
[05:42] Ethan: Back to networking — any suggestion for MTU triage? We can run ping with large packets and DF bit to check PMTU, but pmprobe might be blocked.
[05:52] Connor: Good. Do an IPv4 DF ping and capture with tcpdump. Also check for GRE/encapsulation overhead if you have IPSec tunnel.
[06:02] Sarah: We have IPSec so that explains the 1450 change. But the tunnel endpoint change maybe happened only on one side.
[06:09] Priya: Ok we'll validate both ends.
[06:12] Aisha: Let's set concrete next steps and owners now.
[06:16] Connor: I'll provide the bench harness and a short runbook for packet captures by EOD today.
[06:21] Aisha: Miguel?
[06:22] Miguel: I'll open a Priority-1 support ticket to track the balancing rollout and coordinate the kernel dry-run schedule. I'll also prepare the staged kernel package for your staging pool with rollback instructions.
[06:34] Rajat: When you say dry-run, do you mean we take one staging host at a time? Our staging is 3 hosts; production is 9.
[06:41] Miguel: Yes, rolling single-host dry-run during a low traffic window, verify latency/p95 and KV timings, then proceed to 2-host batch, etc. We'll include healthchecks.
[06:53] Priya: How long is the staging test window? We need to coordinate ML infra jobs that run nightly.
[06:58] Miguel: We'll propose a 60-minute window per host, but we'll respect your job windows and shepherd the test into low-traffic slot.
[07:06] Aisha: Also, Rajat raised earlier about ALB vs NLB choices — NLB TCP preserves client source, but ALB has better health checks. Thoughts?
[07:16] Connor: For streaming workloads we prefer NLB at TCP level to minimize L7 proxies, but ensure health checks are aggressive enough to detect slow worker boot. ALB's keep-alive sometimes hides TCP clogs.
[07:28] Ethan: We can switch health checks to a hybrid: NLB for main traffic, but use ALB path for health diagnostics to trigger faster pullback. It's extra complexity though.
[07:38] Sarah: We want minimal complexity for pilot. Might keep NLB but tune health timeouts.
[07:44] Aisha: Noted.
[07:46] Connor: Quick note on KV cache: Priya, can you send your current cache size and TTLs? The bench will test a few settings to replicate miss storms.
[07:57] Priya: I'll share the config after the call.
[08:00] Rajat: Also want to know about debug logs overhead. When we hit high debug log levels, CPU goes up and schedules shift. Could that affect p95?
[08:10] Miguel: Yes, debug logging can cause lock contention if logs sync to disk. We'll recommend async logging for production.
[08:18] Aisha: Ok moving on — can we review the timeline for the next 72 hours?
[08:22] Connor: Today: bench harness + runbook (Connor) and packet capture instructions. Tomorrow: run bench on staging with TTL variations (TheraScale). Tomorrow EOD: Redwood to analyze logs and propose kernel tweak or config rollback. Day after tomorrow: dry-run kernel on single staging host (Miguel coordinates).
[08:44] Sarah: Sounds tight but doable.
[08:46] Aisha: Any blockers?
[08:47] Rajat: Need the bench script; also need a quick sign-off on the "no-remote-fallback-without-cmk-share" flag from our security team.
[08:56] Aisha: We'll attach the policy draft to the ticket.
[08:58] [10:00] — ten minute jump —
[10:00] Priya: Connor, one more thing: in your lab you mentioned a telemetry metric for KV serialization latency — what's the metric name so we can check it on our side?
[10:10] Connor: It's redwood.kv.serialize.latency_p95 and redwood.kv.fetch.count_miss. We'll add both to the dashboard you have.
[10:20] Sarah: Great. If we see serialize.p95 go up during the bench it's likely kernel; if network retransmit spikes then it's MTU.
[10:28] Miguel: Also add tcp_retransmits and if possible the retransmit timeout histogram.
[10:33] Ethan: We'll set those alerts.
[10:36] Aisha: Any competitor mentions? Rajat previously said they're also evaluating 'CloudAI endpoints' and 'FastServe' — do we need to address comparisons?
[10:47] Rajat: Just FYI, procurement is doing side-by-side on pricing and SLA. We're primarily focusing on stability now.
[10:55] Aisha: Understood. We'll avoid sales pitch in these triages. Focus on engineering.
[11:00] Connor: Final note: when you run the bench, please capture both client-side traces and server-side bprof dumps when you have a repro. Sampling at 100ms resolution helps.
[11:11] Priya: Will do.
[11:13] Aisha: Let's recap action items and close.
[11:17] Aisha: Connor to upload bench harness and runbook by EOD today.
[11:21] Connor: Yep.
[11:22] Aisha: Miguel to open support ticket and prepare staged kernel package + rollback docs.
[11:27] Miguel: I'll create ticket REDWOOD-TSL-112 and invite all.
[11:31] Aisha: TheraScale (Rajat/Ethan/Priya) to run tcpdump and bench in staging, capture logs and share pcaps.
[11:38] Rajat: We'll target tomorrow 01:00-03:00 UTC low traffic window, confirm after the call.
[11:45] Lina: I'll follow up with the security ping for CMK policy.
[11:47] Aisha: Great, we'll reconvene next week same time unless we need an interim deep-dive. Thanks all.
[11:54] Sarah: Thanks.
[11:56] [End 42:00]
